title: Create and use a custom component
summary: Build an attachable rotation behavior, then pause and remove it without recreating its entity.
outcome: A rotating tile with a component that can pause, resume and detach.

blocks.text: A Turntable component updates the transform of any compatible entity. The scene owns the tile; the component owns its behavior. Click the tile to toggle enabled in the complete lab.
update receives elapsed time and delta time in milliseconds. Convert dt to seconds for a speed specified in radians per second. Use the supplied delta instead of assuming a fixed frame rate.

addComponent sets entity before calling onInit. The entity may still be detached from a scene, so onInit cannot assume a device or composer exists. Pass dependencies explicitly or wait for attachment. enabled controls update calls; it does not allocate another component.

The lab enables continuous updates so the component receives frames while the scene has no scheduled animation. Setting enabled to false freezes rotation. Removing a component also removes it from the optimized update list.

Use onInit for subscriptions that only require the entity. Retain listener removers and task handles, then release them in onDestroy. The uniform-shader lesson shows a BufferOwner component for allocations. Changing plain behavior parameters needs no shader rebuild; GPU-facing components must maintain their version and shaderVersion contracts. See [Component](/api-core#component).

items: Replace the click toggle with removeComponent, then attach a fresh instance.
Attach the same behavior type to two different tiles using separate instances.

blocks.text: Check the result: A disabled component should stop rotating while remaining queryable. If all frames stop, inspect continuous rendering and invalidation.
Continue with [Write a custom shader](/tutorial-custom-shader). Use the [tutorial index](/tutorials) to choose another project.
